rows.subtype: Approach: test skills without the tool to catch dependence [Revision]
rows.description: After realising it is hard to write a paragraph unaided, the person schedules tool-free practice and a weekly self-test. Measuring the skill reveals overreliance early.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: ask the tool to critique rather than write [Thinking]
rows.description: A student writes a draft and asks the tool for gaps in reasoning, then fixes them personally. Using AI as a reviewer keeps authorship and improves the work.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: critical path, impulsive action, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: share personal data freely with the chatbot [Pitfall]
rows.description: The person pastes bank statements and a friend's private messages to get help. The data may be stored or reused, and the friend never agreed to this, so privacy is compromised.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: critical path, impulsive action

rows.subtype: Approach: pause and avoid replying in the heat of the moment [Thinking]
rows.description: After a badly received post, the student sees hundreds of hostile comments and decides to wait a day before responding. A delay lets emotion drop and stops a reply that fuels the storm.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: experiment and measure, forward planning, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: reply to every critic to set things straight [Pitfall]
rows.description: The person answers one comment after another through the night, and each reply attracts new attacks and screenshots. Engagement feeds the pile-on and exhausts the person.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, experiment and measure, forward planning, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: lock accounts, mute and save evidence of threats [Action]
rows.description: The person sets accounts private, mutes keywords, saves screenshots of abusive messages and reports them to the platform. Protection and records come before any public statement.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, experiment and measure, forward planning, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: inform trusted people and lean on them [Action]
rows.description: The student tells parents and two close friends what is happening and asks a friend to monitor the accounts for a few days. Sharing the load reduces isolation and bad decisions.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, experiment and measure, forward planning

rows.subtype: Approach: report threats to the cybercrime cell and the college [Action]
rows.description: When comments include threats and the personal address, the student files a complaint with the cybercrime portal and informs the college authorities. Serious threats belong with authorities, not with a fight online.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, experiment and measure, forward planning, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: assess whether the criticism holds a fair point [Thinking]
rows.description: After the intensity fades, the student reads a few measured critiques and asks whether the original post was careless. If there is a real error, a short and sincere correction is the only public response needed.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, forward planning, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: delete everything and vanish to escape [Pitfall]
rows.description: Overwhelmed, the person deletes all accounts and stops going to class. Escape brings short relief but loses evidence and leaves the fear unaddressed.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, experiment and measure, forward planning, seeking advice
